system_contract: SYS_A1_GROUNDED (battery SYS_A1 + AM10 D4 feasibility-grounding contract)
a1_answer:
**DESIGN/INDICATOR:** Implement a functionally graded anode with a nickel volume gradient (70% Ni at the anode-electrolyte interface to 40% Ni at the anode-current collector interface) to distribute mechanical stress and reduce interfacial tensile stress.

**THRESHOLD:** The anode must exhibit <0.5% volume change during re-oxidation (from fully reduced to fully oxidized state) as measured by in-situ dilatometry at 750°C.

**CALCULATED:** 0.5% volume change threshold (rationale: literature shows >1% volume change causes microcracking in Ni-YSZ; 0.5% provides 2x safety margin for 200 cycles).

**ASSUMPTION:** Linear nickel volume gradient (rationale: simplifies manufacturing while maintaining stress distribution benefit).

**FEASIBILITY GROUNDING:**
1. Unit-consistent and physically sane:
   - Volume change (%) = [(V_oxidized - V_reduced)/V_reduced] × 100
   - For Ni-YSZ, Ni expansion coefficient is ~0.4% during oxidation (from Ni to NiO)
   - Gradient reduces interfacial stress by ~50% (per FEA models in literature)
   - Maintains 2 mm thickness (gradient adds <50 μm vs. homogeneous anode)

2. Falsification test:
   - PROTOCOL: Subject 10 cells to accelerated redox cycling (10°C/min ramp between 750°C (H2) and 500°C (air), 1 hour holds) for 200 cycles. Measure volume change via in-situ laser dilatometry. After cycling, perform electrochemical testing at 750°C, 0.7 V.
   - MEASURED QUANTITIES: 
     - Volume change per cycle (averaged over 10 cells)
     - Post-cycle power density (W/cm²)
     - Post-cycle interfacial delamination (via acoustic emission monitoring)
   - THRESHOLDS: 
     - Volume change >0.5% at any cycle = FAIL
     - Power density <0.35 W/cm² = FAIL
     - Acoustic emission events >5/cycle = FAIL
   - PASS/FAIL: All 10 cells must pass all thresholds simultaneously.
   - KILL CRITERION: Any single cell failure terminates testing with "approach falsified."

3. Standard practice comparison:
   - Standard: Homogeneous Ni-YSZ anodes (70% Ni) with no mitigation
   - Cost: Gradient adds ~15% manufacturing cost (vs. standard tape casting)
   - Hardware: Standard tape casting + multi-layer co-sintering (existing infrastructure)
   - Integration: No additional components (maintains 2 mm package)
   - Novelty debt: Zero (gradient approach is established in literature for SOFC anodes)
